title: ROLLUP, CUBE, and GROUPING SETS
description: Generate hierarchical subtotals and cross-tabulated aggregates in a single query using ROLLUP, CUBE, and GROUPING SETS.

data.text: Sometimes a single GROUP BY is not enough. You might want subtotals per region, per category, and a grand total — all in one report. Rather than running four separate queries, SQL Server lets you generate multiple grouping sets in a single pass using ROLLUP, CUBE, and GROUPING SETS.

A *grouping set* is a specific combination of columns that you group by. A plain GROUP BY (brand, category) defines one grouping set: (brand, category). But you might also want subtotals by brand alone, by category alone, and an overall grand total. That is four grouping sets:

data.title: Four grouping sets we might want
data.content:
(brand, category) — detail level
(brand) — subtotal per brand
(category) — subtotal per category
() — grand total across everything

data.text: GROUPING SETS lets you list exactly which combinations you want. You list each grouping set as a parenthesized list of columns inside the GROUPING SETS clause.

data.title: Explicit grouping sets
data.code:
SELECT
    brand,
    category,
    SUM(sales) AS sales
FROM   sales.sales_summary
GROUP BY
    GROUPING SETS (
        (brand, category),  -- detail level
        (brand),            -- subtotal by brand
        (category),         -- subtotal by category
        ()                  -- grand total
    )
ORDER BY brand, category;

data.title: NULL in the output
data.text: In a grouping set that does not include a column, SQL Server fills that column's place with NULL. To distinguish a real NULL from a 'subtotal' NULL, use the GROUPING() function.

ROLLUP assumes a hierarchy among the dimension columns and generates subtotals at each level. For ROLLUP(brand, category), it produces (brand, category), then (brand), then the grand total (). It is perfect for drill-down reports: year → quarter → month → day.

data.title: ROLLUP for hierarchical subtotals
data.code:
SELECT
    brand,
    category,
    SUM(sales) AS sales
FROM   sales.sales_summary
GROUP BY ROLLUP(brand, category);

rows: Grand total across all brands and categories

data.title: Column order in ROLLUP matters
data.text: ROLLUP(brand, category) is NOT the same as ROLLUP(category, brand). The first argument is the highest level in the hierarchy. Choose the order to match your reporting hierarchy: region → state → city, not city → region.
CUBE generates every possible combination of the dimension columns. For N columns, that is 2^N grouping sets. It is exhaustive — use it when you want a full cross-tab of subtotals.

data.title: CUBE with 2 dimensions = 4 grouping sets
data.code:
SELECT
    brand,
    category,
    SUM(sales) AS sales
FROM   sales.sales_summary
GROUP BY CUBE(brand, category);

data.caption: With 2 columns, CUBE produces 4 grouping sets; ROLLUP produces only 3 (no category-only subtotal)

data.text: GROUPING(column) returns 1 if the column's value is NULL because it was aggregated (i.e., it's a subtotal row), and 0 otherwise. This lets you label your output so you can tell detail rows apart from subtotal rows.

data.title: Labeling subtotal rows
data.code:
SELECT
    CASE WHEN GROUPING(brand) = 1 THEN 'ALL BRANDS'
         ELSE brand END  AS brand,
    CASE WHEN GROUPING(category) = 1 THEN 'ALL CATEGORIES'
         ELSE category END AS category,
    SUM(sales) AS sales
FROM   sales.sales_summary
GROUP BY GROUPING SETS (
    (brand, category), (brand), (category), ()
);

data.title: Choosing the right tool
points: GROUPING SETS — explicit control; list exactly the combinations you need
ROLLUP — hierarchical subtotals (n, n-1, ..., grand total); fewer grouping sets than CUBE
CUBE — every combination; powerful but can be slow on many columns
GROUPING() tells you whether a NULL is a real value or an aggregated subtotal
For reporting: ROLLUP for drill-downs, CUBE for full cross-tabs, GROUPING SETS for custom
